reason: Process snapshot and text describe solution treatment of austenite based duplex steels before water quenching.
Solution treatment is a thermal (heat treatment) step applied to austenite based duplex steels.
The sample is 'solution treated'; text states cold rolled strips of austenitic/duplex steels are solution treated in the single austenite phase area at 900-1100 °C.
General processing text states solution treatment range 900-1100 °C; specific austenite based duplex examples use 1050 °C.
Temperatures reported in °C.
Table 4 gives solution treatment 1050 °C/25 min for the SIP Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C alloy; b0195 gives solution treatment at 1050 °C for Fe-27Mn-11.5Al-0.95C.
Processing text and specific alloy examples give the solution treatment condition.
Water quenching is the final cooling step of the defined process (proc_austenite-duplex-st-wq).
Water quenching is the rapid cooling step that defines the ST+WQ sample state.
Text: the strips are solution treated and then quenched in water, oil or other quench media; specific example 'solution treatment at 1050 °C and water quenching'.
Cooling medium is water (water quenching).
Fast cooling/water quenching is used to avoid formation of coarse intergranular κ-carbides.
Text states austenitic/duplex steels are water quenched from solution treatment to avoid coarse κ-carbide formation, and ST+WQ austenite contains SROs/nano κ'-carbides.

b0048 defines austenite based duplex (triplex) steels as γ+δ at hot working temperature with austenite as continuous matrix, containing small amounts of δ-ferrite and intragranular nano-sized κ-carbides.
Triplex steels contain three constituents: austenite matrix + small δ-ferrite + intragranular nano-sized κ-carbides.
Overall microstructure of the ST+WQ austenite based duplex steel.
Microstructure is that of the sample after solution treatment and water quenching (step 2).
Austenite forms the continuous matrix of austenite based duplex steels.
Austenite is FCC; κ is an ordered FCC derivative of the γ matrix.
The austenitic phase forms the continuous matrix in austenite based duplex steels.
Austenite forms continuous matrix; duplex hot-rolled microstructure shows thin strip-like δ and γ.
γ grain size ~30 μm for Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C (Table 4) and ~50 μm for Fe-27Mn-11.5Al-0.95C after ST+WQ.
δ-ferrite is the second (minor) phase of austenite based duplex steels.
δ-ferrite has BCC structure; at high Al it forms ordered B2 and DO3 domains.
b0194 gives 6-8% ferrite for Fe-(26-28)Mn-(10-12)Al-(1.0-1.2)C triplex; Table 4 gives 8% δ; b0195 gives 6% δ; b0196 gives ~21% δ.
Hot-rolled duplex microstructure shows δ-ferrite stringers/bands parallel to rolling direction.
γ grain size ~30 μm (Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C, Table 4) and ~50 μm (Fe-27Mn-11.5Al-0.95C).
Intragranular nano-sized κ-carbides are the third constituent of triplex steels; κ has perovskite E2_1 structure; metastable κ'-(Fe,Mn)3AlCx (x<1).
Table 4 gives as-quenched microstructure γ + 8% δ + κ' (20-30 nm) for the SIP Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C alloy.
Intragranular κ'-carbides are produced homogeneously within the austenitic matrix.
κ'-carbide is coherent with the matrix; cube-on-cube orientation relationship with lattice misfit less than 3%.
